unit.why: A short anecdote: the Maggid of Kozhnitz, coming back from his son R. Motele's funeral, says something that frames the death as a harsh 'betrothal slap' from Heaven. The narrator heard it from R. Meir Shalom.

stories.end_quote: אז א צאהן פאלט איהר א ויס
stories.summary_en: After the death of his son R. Motele, the Maggid of Kozhnitz returns from the funeral and compares his loss to a western betrothal custom, in which the bride is acquired by a slap hard enough to knock out a tooth.

quotes: אשר בעת שהלך לעולמו הרה״צ מו"ה מאטילי
tags.why: The death of the Maggid's son is the triggering event.
The tzaddik's son is the one who dies.

quotes: סיפר לי ש"ב ב"ד הרב הצדיק המפו'
tags.why: The tale is framed as told to the narrator by R. Meir Shalom in Kaloshin.

quotes: בארצות המערב המנהג אצלם שקנין וקידושי אשה
tags.why: The core of the story is a mashal the Maggid tells to interpret his bereavement.

quotes: שקנין וקידושי אשה לאיש נגמר ע"י שיתן
tags.why: A betrothal custom is the imagery of the parable.

quotes: עהר גיט אטראסק אז א צאהן פאלט
tags.why: A wry, bitter witty remark in the face of grief.
The bride in the parable is mentioned only.

missing_concepts: bereavement / a tzaddik's response to the death of a child
suffering as a sign of divine love (yissurin shel ahavah)
